primary.title: The Code of Hammurabi
primary.author: Hammurabi
primary.rationale: The most famous and significant primary source attributed to Hammurabi, containing laws and judgments. It is widely available in translation.

secondary.title: The Laws of Ancient Mesopotamia
secondary.author: Marc Van De Mieroop
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive academic study of Mesopotamian law, including detailed analysis of Hammurabi's code within its historical context. Van De Mieroop is a respected Assyriologist.

secondary.title: Hammurabi: King of Babylon
secondary.author: John L. Hayes
secondary.rationale: A scholarly biography and analysis of Hammurabi's reign and the significance of his legal code. Hayes is a recognized scholar in the field.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to Ancient Mesopotamia
secondary.author: Edited by Amanda H. Podany and Karen Radner
secondary.rationale: This collection includes scholarly chapters on various aspects of Mesopotamian history and culture, with likely contributions discussing Hammurabi and his code.

suggestions.notes: Hammurabi himself did not author texts in the modern sense; the Code of Hammurabi is a compilation of laws issued during his reign and attributed to him. Primary source availability is based on common translations of the Code.
